chunks: He said: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad - may God have mercy on him - reported to me from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Musa ibn Talha, from Abu Muhammad the brother of Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from his brother Yunus, who said:

I was in Medina when Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, met me in one of its lanes. He said: "Go, O Yunus, for indeed at the door is a man from us, the Ahl al-Bayt." He said: So I went to the door and there was Isa ibn Abdillah sitting. I said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am a man from the people of Qum." He said: No sooner than Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, came on a donkey and entered the house on the donkey. Then he turned to us and said: "Enter, both of you."

Then he said: "O Yunus, I believe you objected to my statement to you that Isa ibn Abdillah is from us, the Ahl al-Bayt?" He said: I said: "Yes, by God, may I be your ransom, because Isa ibn Abdillah is a man from the people of Qum, so how can he be from you, the Ahl al-Bayt?" He said: "O Yunus, Isa ibn Abdillah is a man from us while alive, and he is from us after death."

key_terms.أهل البيت: Ahl al-Bayt - the Prophet's household; here used in a spiritual sense to include devoted followers
key_terms.المدينة: Medina - the city of the Prophet in the Hijaz region
key_terms.جعلت فداك: May I be your ransom - a respectful expression of devotion used when addressing the Imams

ai.seo_question: Can someone outside the Prophet's lineage be considered part of Ahl al-Bayt according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narrative, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches Yunus ibn Ya'qub that the spiritual bond of wilayah transcends lineage and geography. The Imam declares that Isa ibn Abdillah, a man from Qum with no blood connection to the Prophet's household, is counted among the Ahl al-Bayt both in life and after death, emphasizing that true belonging to the Ahl al-Bayt is defined by faith and devotion rather than mere genealogy.
